Dataset brief description: An open RDF knowledge graph containing data from citizen deliberation and participation processes

Dataset name: Citizen science for traffic counts: WeCount project dataset for inner-city streets of Ljubljana
Dataset brief description: Traffic counts gathered in Ljubljana as part of the WeCount initiative are included in an open citizen science dataset. In addition to helping with data collecting and analysis, participating residents put inexpensive traffic sensors in their homes or places of business. The dataset can be found in semantic formats such as RDF/XML and JSON-LD and is publicly accessible.

Multilingual lexical resource extracted from Wiktionary and published as Linguistic Linked Open Data in RDF with the W3C OntoLex-Lemon vocabulary. Covers 27 Wiktionary language editions, is re-extracted twice a month, and offers Turtle dumps plus a public SPARQL endpoint. The content is written and curated by volunteer Wiktionary contributors, not by any public administration. License CC BY-SA 3.0.

Cultural Gems is a crowdsourced platform for mapping cultural and creative places across European cities. Its data are contributed and curated by community members, culture lovers and other users. The resulting dataset is published as Linked Open Data in RDF formats by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission

A citizen-generated biodiversity dataset containing research-grade observations contributed by iNaturalist users, where people share observations of plants, animals and other organisms from around the world.

Crowdsourced database of food products worldwide, built and curated by volunteer contributors who scan and upload product data via mobile app (citizen-generated, not government data). Provides open data exports in multiple formats including an RDF distribution, alongside CSV and a live JSON API.

Weekly-updated RDF (Turtle) conversion of the entire OpenStreetMap planet dataset, including precomputed spatial relations between objects, generated and maintained by volunteer citizen mappers worldwide (not by any government agency), queryable via a live SPARQL endpoint at qlever.dev/osm-planet.
A crowdsourced Linked Data entity from Wikidata mapping the architectural heritage of the Palladian Villas in the Veneto region, collaboratively curated by citizens and available natively in RDF.

A crowdsourced linguistic library where citizens record audio of words and phrases in various languages and dialects. The platform's structured metadata is modeled as a Wikibase knowledge graph, making it queryable via SPARQL as Linked Open Data.

Dataset name: Citizen Science Spider Records for Ireland
Dataset brief description: Citizen-generated records of spider species collected through citizen science across the island of Ireland between 2011 and 2020.
A community-built database of ancient historical places, created by volunteers and available as Linked Open Data in RDF format.

Dataset name: Problems registered by users on the “Manage the City” platform in Vilnius City Municipality
Dataset brief description: User reports of problems in Vilnius, including their type, status, location, and resolution details

Collaborative open dataset containing food product information contributed and maintained by citizens, including ingredients, nutritional values, brands and labels. The dataset is also available in RDF.

This dataset contains hourly air pollution measurements in Alcobendas, Spain, for 2024. It has 85.822 records and 8 variables, covering 10 different pollutants. The main variables include the date and hour of measurement, pollutant type, concentration, measurement units, and pollutant classification. The pollutants include PM10, ozone (O_3), NO_2, NO, benzene, toluene, xylenes, and hydrocarbons. The dataset can be used to analyse hourly and seasonal patterns in air pollution and compare pollutant concentrations over time.
Locations of toilets in The Hague accessible to disabled people

OpenHistoricalMap is a volunteer-mapped database documenting how the geography of the world has changed over time, covering historical borders, settlements, transport networks and place names, each annotated with its validity dates. Available in RDF Turtle and through a public SPARQL endpoint.
Citizen-generated dataset of aurora observations, including information on the observation time and location, sky conditions, aurora colors and types, duration, and images.
This dataset shows the UFO sightings. It contains data from the past and well as the recent years. The time, place, season, country code and precise date has been included in the dataset
Dataset containing information about municipally owned dog areas in Madrid, including their location, surface area, and availability of play equipment for dogs.

"Citizen-curated semantic wiki (Semantic MediaWiki) of human SNPs, genotypes and their medical/phenotypic associations, contributed by direct-to-consumer genetic testing users and citizen scientists."
A citizen science dataset that collects participants' responses about their motivations for taking part in participatory research projects

Cultural Gems is a crowdsourced dataset of cultural and creative places in European cities and towns. The information is contributed by the community and the dataset follows Linked Open Data principles, providing data in RDF and other semantic formats.
Linked Open Data dataset of archaeological artifacts discovered and reported by citizen scientists in Finland.

The Cinema Context RDF dataset is a Linked Data representation converted from MySQL data of the Dutch Cinema Context. It uses RDF and Semantic Web vocabularies such as Schema.org, with links to external resources including IMDb and Wikidata, and is distributed in TriG format for SPARQL-based querying.

Dataset brief description: Explores the neurobehavioral factors related to eating disorders among university students in Bangladesh

An open, community-curated music encyclopedia where volunteer editors add and correct data on artists, albums, and recordings. Each entity has a persistent URI that natively returns Linked Data (JSON-LD) via content negotiation.
Citizen-submitted photos and location data of wild species, cross-checked and labeled by public users
Measurements and RDF provenance graphs analyzing OpenStreetMap data, a crowdsourced and citizen-generated mapping project created by worldwide volunteer contributors.
